findings.statement: CXCR2 is the top convergence gene: pooled UC vs control log2FC is [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.264], with an increase in all five cohorts. It is local to inflamed mucosa, with a paired inflamed vs non-inflamed log2FC of [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972]. Caveat: CXCR2 is mainly a neutrophil receptor, so the bulk signal probably reflects neutrophil infiltration rather than a change in tissue cells.

Non-inflamed UC mucosa in MSCCR also shows a small but significant CXCR2 rise versus control, with log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.6399]. This is much smaller than in inflamed tissue, so the signal is mostly a marker of local inflammation.

CXCL8 (IL-8), the main CXCR1/CXCR2 ligand, is strongly and reproducibly up, with a pooled log2FC of [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.7037], significant in all five cohorts. Together with CXCL1 and CXCL5 and the receptors CXCR1 and CXCR2, it forms a coherent neutrophil-recruitment axis. The source is partly infiltrating myeloid cells and partly epithelium, so cell composition must be resolved.

CHI3L1 has one of the largest pooled increases, log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.7135], upregulated in all five cohorts. It is also mildly raised in non-inflamed mucosa, with log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.8377]. It therefore behaves as both an inflammation marker and a marker of the disease state.

DUOX2 is an epithelial innate-defence gene with a pooled log2FC of [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.3213] in five of five cohorts. The paired inflamed vs non-inflamed log2FC is [gene=DUOX2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.4812]. DUOXA2 shows the same pattern. Both are good local-inflammation markers, and the epithelial origin makes them less likely to come from infiltrating cells.

HMGCS2, an epithelial ketogenesis and metabolism gene, is lost in UC, with a pooled log2FC of [gene=HMGCS2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-3.5845] in all five cohorts. It is not changed in non-inflamed MSCCR mucosa (padj [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; padj=0.675]). The loss is therefore specific to inflamed tissue. This fits a biomarker of epithelial inflammation, not a drug target.

CLDN8, a tight-junction gene, is the most strongly lost gene in the pooled analysis, with log2FC [gene=CLDN8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-4.518] and a decrease in all five cohorts. It indicates epithelial barrier loss and is a biomarker candidate, not a target.

IDO1 (tryptophan catabolism, immune regulation) is strongly up, with a pooled log2FC of [gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.445] across five cohorts. It looks like an interferon-driven feedback program. Because IDO1 is expressed in myeloid and epithelial cells and infiltrating immune cells, the bulk rise needs a cell-composition check.

CD274 (PD-L1) is also reproducibly up, with a pooled log2FC of [gene=CD274; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.887]. Like IDO1, it looks like an interferon-driven feedback program, and its bulk rise needs a cell-composition check.

JAK2 ranks high on genetic and tractability streams, but its expression change is modest, with a pooled log2FC of [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.872]. It is significant in all five cohorts, but the effect is small compared with the chemokines and matrix metalloproteinases. Its rank reflects genetics and drug availability more than a large expression change in the tissue.

OSMR, the receptor for oncostatin M, is up in UC with a pooled log2FC of [gene=OSMR; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.042] and is local to inflamed mucosa. The paired inflamed vs non-inflamed log2FC is [gene=OSMR; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=0.8848]. This supports the OSM-OSMR axis as an inflamed-tissue pathway, and the stromal or immune origin of the signal remains to be resolved.

MMP3 is among the strongest up genes, with a pooled log2FC of [gene=MMP3; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.642] across five cohorts. MMP1, MMP7, MMP9 and MMP10 follow the same pattern. This is a tissue-remodelling signature that works well as a marker, but broad MMP inhibitors have a poor record as therapy.

S100A8 (with S100A9 and LCN2) is strongly up, with a pooled log2FC of [gene=S100A8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.647] in all five cohorts. It is a calprotectin-type neutrophil marker, and its rise most likely reflects infiltrating neutrophils. This makes it a marker of inflammatory activity and not evidence of a change in tissue cells.

CCL2 has a pooled log2FC of [gene=CCL2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.28]. It was measured in only four cohorts, all significantly up, and the data returned no record for the fifth cohort, GSE73661. Its paired inflamed signal is weaker than for the neutrophil chemokines, so it is a less specific marker of local inflammation.

caveats: Bulk biopsy data: increases in immune genes (CXCR1, CXCR2, CXCL8, S100A8/9, IDO1, CD274) may come from infiltrating neutrophils and myeloid cells and not from a change inside the tissue; deconvolution is pending.
Microarray fold changes are compressed relative to RNA-seq; compare directions and significance across cohorts, not sizes.
Between-cohort heterogeneity (I2) is high for most top genes, so pooled log2FC values describe direction and rough size only.
Non-inflamed vs control and paired contrasts exist only in MSCCR; replication of the local-inflammation pattern in the microarray cohorts was not tested.
Some genes (SLC6A14, DEFB4A, SAA2) are measured in few cohorts, so they were not prioritised; CCL2 lacks a record in one cohort.
Genetics, literature and tractability scores come from the ranking and were not independently evaluated here.
